title: Add CI cache layers and a wall-time-per-result baseline measurement
summary: Reads "build the routing" as the first buildable slice of docs/design/ci-routing.md section 10: the baseline measurement (item 2) plus the CI cache layers (item 3) in ci.yml, for the owner and the design reviewers. It records a measured "before" and a repeatable computation for "after". The SHA-keyed result reuse and per-kind routing (items 4-5) are left to later jobs.

defaults_applied.how: Measurement code is a Rust xtask subcommand, not a script.
The measurement code has unit tests; cargo test and clippy pass.
Numbers are measured or labeled estimate/given.
Only the baseline and cache slices are built.
Criteria check wall time per verified result is computed, not that a workflow exists.
Criteria exercise the computation on sample records.
Policy tests, if any exist for workflows, are run and kept passing.
Verifier runs cargo test and the new xtask command.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The request authorizes building despite the pending review in docs/design/reviews/ci-routing-review-1.md; the producer must not edit that review or mark the design accepted.
'Small' default applies: only build-plan items 2 (baseline) and 3 (cache) are built; items 4-7 are later jobs.
'Before' is computed from existing job records or, if per-phase timestamps are absent, reported as unavailable with the requester's ~25 min median labeled given, not measured.
'After' cannot be measured in this job; the change provides the repeatable computation and a stated procedure, and the doc says so.
Cache actions are pinned by SHA like the existing workflow actions; only the default branch saves the target cache.
question: The design says no build starts before review 1 is recorded, and the review's verdict is still "Pending". Does your request override that gate? I assumed it does, and that you want only the first slice built.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run cargo test --locked: all tests pass, including new tests showing the wall-time computation gives the median and p90 of dispatch-to-verified time on sample records, reports failed/rejected jobs separately, and states when fewer than 20 jobs exist.
Run cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all --check: both clean.

Run the new xtask command via cargo run --locked -p xtask on the repository's job records or sample fixture: it prints wall time per verified result by job kind, or says explicitly that the records lack the timestamps instead of printing zero or an empty success.
A baseline document gives the before figures with each number marked measured, given or estimate, and states how to compute the after figures with the same command and N=20.

ci.yml adds toolchain, registry and target cache layers keyed on rust-toolchain.toml and Cargo.lock as in design 4.1, with the cache action pinned by SHA, target saved only on the default branch, and the cache outcome (exact, restore key, miss) reported.
ci.yml still runs the same checks (xtask ci and the history job) with unchanged permissions; no check is removed or skipped. ci.yml is named as a changed governance path in the change notes.
docs/design/ci-routing.md is not marked accepted, the review file is unchanged, and the CHANGELOG records what was built and what remains (build-plan items 4-7).

out_of_scope: SHA-keyed CI result reuse and local fallback (build-plan item 4)
Editing athena.toml, defaults.toml, or the review file
departures: Larger than the reference: the request spans a workflow change, new Rust measurement code with tests, and a baseline document, and it conflicts with the design's own review gate.
